wholeAssessmentRequirements: Treat general 0<p_n<1 with p_n→0 and n p_n→lambda>0, for every fixed integer k≥0; a proof restricted to p_n=lambda/n is not the whole canonical competence.
Show binomial mass factorization into (n p_n)^k/k! times product_j(1-j/n) times (1-p_n)^n times (1-p_n)^(-k), with empty product at k=0.

Explain each limiting factor. Supply permitted elementary limit facts, e.g. log(1-x)/x→-1 and continuity of exp, and ordinary limit algebra so no undeclared analysis course is silently required. Show n log(1-p_n)=(n p_n)(log(1-p_n)/p_n)→-lambda.

Conclude lambda^k exp(-lambda)/k! and explain fixed-k pointwise statement, rare independent trials, approximately constant mean and finite-n approximation limits. If normalization is requested, provide exponential-series identity rather than add an undeclared analysis proof.
Include a small numerical rare-event application/comparison and explain that the finite binomial and Poisson distributions are not exactly identical.

Use one ordinary total-score rubric and one binary pass. A normal holistic proof-core score cap may prevent passing without any genuine limit derivation; no prerequisite coverage attestations or all-R pass predicates. Equivalent proofs and fair follow-through must be accepted.
